newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Galileo to acquire Traviswiss after IPO.
newsitem.headline: Galileo to acquire Traviswiss after IPO.

text.p: Galileo International, an electronic reservations company owned by several airlines, will acquire Traviswiss, the leading reservation system in Switzerland owned by SAirGroup.

SAirGroup, which includes the Swissair airline, said the acquisition was part of the integration of national distribution companies into Galileo's global distribution system and would take place after an initial public offering (IPO) of Galileo shares this summer.

Traviswiss is Switzerland's leading reservation system with an 80 percent share of the market. The company, which employs 53 people, provides travel agents with reservation services, hardware, software and technical assistance.
Galileo has already said that it will buy Apollo Travel Services, 77 percent owned by United Airlines, a unit of Chicago-based UAL Corp.
Apollo markets Galileo's computer reservation services in the United States, Mexico, and the Caribbean.
SAirGroup currently owns 13.2 percent of Galileo, but this stake will be reduced to seven percent after the IPO.
Other current major shareholders in Galileo are United United Airlines with 38 percent, British Airways with 14.7 percent, KLM with 12.1 percent, US Airways and Alitalia with 8.7 percent.
